doc: Every file or folder the mashup reads or writes. 'guarded' means it must never be modified by the mashup; tests assert it.

rows.purpose: The player's real Dark Souls III saves: read for the copy and the hash check only; restored from backup if it ever changes
Full copy of the real save taken before each launch (newest three kept)
The mashup's private copy of the save; the game's save folder is redirected here
The game; started only through ModEngine2, never modified
ModEngine2's launcher, installed by Melty
ModEngine2's injected library, installed by Melty
ModEngine2 config generated before every launch: our hook DLL and mod folder
Generated before every launch: tells the hook DLL the real and private save folders and the log path
The hook DLL ModEngine2 loads into the game
ModEngine2 mod folder (loose game-file overrides); empty in milestone 1
What the hook DLL did this session
What the launcher did this session
The player's Space Marine 2 install: read-only, never written, never launched
SM2 content converted on the player's PC; private, never uploaded or committed
What the read-only game probe found (also probe-ds3-weapons.csv, -goods.csv, -inventory.csv, -samples.csv, -text-*.csv next to it)

A read-only look at ModEngine2's footprint in the running game: where its file hook and patches should be in the program file and what is there (bytes, where a jump leads), and how often its loose-parameter signatures occur
The setup tool's probe report and texture preview pictures (private; made from the player's own install)
Optional: the player's Space Marine 2 folder on its first line, when it is not in a normal Steam library
WAV files made on the player's PC from their own Space Marine 2 sound files (private; never uploaded or committed)
Written last by the setup tool: says the conversion finished and what it made
What the setup tool converted, with the sound-container trees it followed (private)
Lists the sound slots and their WAV files; read by the hook DLL when the game starts
Dark Souls III's own archives (Data*.bhd, Data*.bdt, DLC*.bhd/.bdt), opened read-only by ds3-probe and ds3-prepare to read the item text; nothing in this folder is ever changed
What ds3-probe / ds3-prepare found in the game's archives and what they wrote (private; key fingerprints only, no keys)

Loose copy of the game's English item text with the test weapons' names, picked up by ModEngine2 instead of the archived file. This is the file a fully updated game asks ModEngine2 for (kits 0.5 to 0.9 wrote item.msgbnd.dcx, which the game never asks for, so the names never changed)
The same changed copy for an install that asks for the item text of the first downloadable content (written only if the archives hold that file)
The same changed copy for an install without the downloadable content (written only if the archives hold that file)
Which source text the override was made from (hashes) and what it changed, so a stale override is noticed

Only if the exe does not hold the archive keys as plain text: the public RSA keys the running game has in memory (PEM, DER or key blobs; a number found through a big-number structure only if a real archive proves it), written by the test kit's collector while the game runs so ds3-prepare can use them

Every public RSA key the collector saw in the running game's memory, whatever it opened (a few dozen, mostly from the system): ds3-probe and ds3-prepare try each one on the archives that no key has opened yet and say which ones turn the first block into a plain block (kit 0.9)
Where Dark Souls III keeps the files the mod needs (path hashes with the archive they are in, file sizes, a dry run of the name change, the weapon model containers); private, key fingerprints only

The plain table of contents of each archive (<name>.bin), saved by the test kit's collector from the running game's memory when it lies there whole and checks out (parses completely, fits the .bhd, every file inside the .bdt); ds3-prepare uses it when no key opens an archive
What the test kit's collector looked for in the game's memory and what it found (key fingerprints and places only, never key text)
A second set of the same sounds made with the volumes and delays of the game's own sound bank (only when the bank can be read exactly); the in-game key F9 switches between it and the first set

How the chainsword and bolt pistol templates read: objects, detail levels, the merged full-detail sub mesh, its bounds, material and the textures it names with the descriptors found in the paks (names and numbers only, no copies); private

OPTIONAL. Plain copies of the chainsword and bolt pistol template files and of the textures their full-detail material names, made only when the owner runs Send-Model-Files.bat and chooses yes; the owner decides whether to send them; never part of the mashup

OPTIONAL. Plain copies of five Dark Souls III weapon containers (parts/wp_a_0200, _0200_l, _1404, _1409, _1419 .partsbnd.dcx as the game stores them) and ds3-export-report.txt, made only when the owner runs Send-Model-Files.bat and chooses yes; the owner decides whether to send them; never part of the mashup

The weapon containers the model swap writes (a copy of the game's container whose model carries the Space Marine 2 shape); ModEngine2 loads them instead of the archived ones; removed again when anything is wrong so a stale model never stays
What the in-memory rename found and wrote in the running game (addresses, the bytes around each string, results)

Copies of the small table-of-contents files (.bhd) of the archives that could not be opened, and of the public keys the collector saw, for the optional model-files zip: they let the owner of the project see how those archives are laid out (private test kit only)
